title: Sealed holdout of a factory run (holdout.json)
description: Where the sealed holdout lives and how to run it against an integrated tree. The folder holds SEAL (the sha256 of MANIFEST.sha256) and MANIFEST.sha256 (the sha256 of every other file); `seal` here must equal SEAL, so a spec cannot point at a holdout other than the one it names. cmd/factory mounts the folder read-only at /holdout and the checkout read-only at /src, with no network, only while it validates a lane on the integration branch; `command` assembles the checkout and the tests inside the container and its exit code is the verdict. The environment carries HOLDOUT_FILES: the files of the units to run, space separated.

dir.description: Host folder of the sealed holdout. Never inside the checkout that is validated.

command.description: Run with sh -c in the image; /src is the checkout (read-only), /holdout the sealed folder (read-only), the working directory is empty and writable.

units.description: Which holdout files decide which issue. An accepted lane's issue must be listed here; a lane without a unit cannot be integrated.
